translations.title: Rhyme XI: I Am Passionate, I Am Dark-Haired
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXXIII: Dark Phantoms
translations.text:
Dark phantoms,
somber clouds,
flee before the flash
of divine light.
That holy light,
girl with dark eyes,
is hope.

In the warmth of its rays,
my mighty faith
struggles against disdain
without growing less.
In this endeavor,
if the suffering is great,
the reward is greater.

And if you still show me,
elusive one, a soul of snow;
if you still do not love me,
I shall love you.
My love is a rock
against which the timid waves
of the sea break.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XLII: When They Told Me, I Felt the Cold
translations.text:
When they told me, I felt the cold
of a steel blade in my entrails;
I leaned against the wall and for a moment
lost all sense of where I was.

Night fell upon my spirit;
my soul was engulfed in anger and pity...
And then I understood why people weep,
and then I understood why people kill!

The cloud of grief passed... With pain
I managed to stammer a few words...
Who had brought me the news? A faithful friend...
He had done me a great favor! I thanked him.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXVI: Where Do I Come From?
translations.text:
Where do I come from? Seek the most dreadful,
rugged path:
the tracks of bloodied feet
upon hard rock;
the remnants of a soul torn to shreds
among sharp brambles
will tell you the way
that leads to my cradle.

Where am I going? Cross the darkest,
saddest wasteland,
a valley of eternal snows and eternal,
melancholy mists.
Where a solitary stone stands
without an inscription,
where oblivion dwells,
there my grave will be.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XVIII: Weary from the Dance
translations.text:
Weary from the dance,
cheeks flushed, breath short,
leaning on my arm,
she paused at one end of the hall.

Amid the light gauze
lifted by her heaving breast,
a flower swayed
in gentle, measured motion.

As in a mother-of-pearl cradle
rocked by the sea and caressed by the west wind,
perhaps it slept there
in the breath from her parted lips.

Oh, I thought, who could let
time glide by like this?
Oh, if flowers sleep,
what a sweet dream!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XVI: If, as the Blue Bellflowers Sway
translations.text:
If, as the blue bellflowers
on your balcony sway,
you think the murmuring wind
passes with a sigh,
know that, hidden among the green leaves,
it is I who sigh.

If, when a vague sound echoes
behind you,
you think a distant voice
has called your name,
know that, among the shadows around you,
it is I who call.

If in the dead of night
your heart stirs with fear
when you feel a burning breath
upon your lips,
know that, though invisible, beside you
it is I who breathe.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme I: I Know a Strange and Mighty Hymn
translations.text:
I know a strange and mighty hymn
that heralds dawn in the soul's night,
and these pages are cadences of that hymn
that the air carries through the shadows.

I would write it down, taming
humanity's rebellious, meager language,
with words that would be at once
sighs and laughter, colors and notes.

But it is vain to struggle; no sign
can contain it, and I could barely, O beautiful one,
even holding your hands in mine,
tell it to you alone, in your ear.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XLV: On the Keystone of the Unsteady Arch
translations.text:
On the keystone of the unsteady arch,
whose stones time had reddened,
a Gothic coat of arms stood out,
roughly carved by a chisel.

Like the plume of its granite helmet,
the ivy hanging all around
shaded the shield, on which a hand
held a heart.

We both stopped to look at it
in the deserted square,
and she said, “That is the perfect emblem
of my constant love.”

Alas, what she told me then was true.
True that she will carry her heart
in her hand... anywhere at all,
but not in her breast.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXVI: I Go Against My Interests in Confessing It
translations.text:
I go against my interests in confessing it,
but I, my beloved,
agree with you that an ode is good only
when written on the back of a banknote.
Some fool, hearing this,
will surely cross himself and say,
“A woman of the nineteenth century,
materialistic and prosaic...” Nonsense!
Words spread by four poets
who wrap themselves in a lyre in winter!
Dogs barking at the moon!
You and I both know that in this life,
very few can write poetry with genius,
while anyone can make it with gold.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
